name: qjs_new_array_buffer_copy_composition
prototype: JSValue qjs_new_array_buffer_copy(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *data, size_t length)

ownership.argument: No copy wrapper exists on this build, so the module composes it: allocate length bytes through js_malloc_rt 0xC2D10F8, copy the caller data into it, then hand it to js_new_array_buffer 0xC2D34C8, which adopts it and installs the free callback 0xC27369C so the buffer owns the copy. The adoption is what makes the copy mandatory: js_new_array_buffer frees its data pointer with 0xC27369C, so passing the caller buffer directly would free memory the caller owns.

provenance.source: js_new_array_buffer 0xC2D34C8 has exactly two callers (0xC861308, a 28-byte forwarder, and 0xC8712A4, a firmware JS binding) and neither copies; the callee installs sub_C27369C as the free callback unconditionally, which is the signature of the adopt-with-free variant.
